subject: Data Engineering
title: Bill Inmon's Vision
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bill Inmon's Vision.

hook.text: In 1992, Bill Inmon published the book that defined data warehousing. He's called the father of it.

buildup.text: Inmon proposed a centralized, subject-oriented, time-variant, non-volatile data store.

discovery.text: His approach: normalize the warehouse first, then build department-specific data marts on top.

twist.text: Normalization avoids duplication but makes queries complex. Analysts need to join many tables.

climax.text: Inmon's top-down approach works best for large enterprises with strong governance.

punchline.text: Inmon said: build the truth first, then serve it.

quiz.question: What is Bill Inmon's approach to data warehousing?
options: Normalize first, then build department data marts
Skip the warehouse and use data lakes
